sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company seeking exoneration from liability to pay compensation awarded by learned Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Karera, District Shivpuri vide Award dated 19.01.2016 passed in Claim Case No.06 of 2014, whereby a sum of Rs.32,500/- has been awarded in favour of respondent No.1 claimant along with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition, on account of injuries sustained by him in a motor accident.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Karera
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. In brief, the facts giving rise to present appeal are that respondent No.1- claimant filed a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal contending that on 01.02.2012 at about 8.00 p.m., while he was returning to his house after taking dinner with his friend Patiram Lodhi at Rakesh Hotel, a Maruti Van bearing registration No. MP-04-J-5462, being driven by respondent No.2 in a rash and negligent manner and owned by respondent No.3, came from the opposite direction near Rapta and dashed against the claimant, causing grievous injuries.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28093 2 MA-379-2016 The matter was reported to Police Station- Amola on 07.02.2012 and an offence was registered.

It was submitted that the offending vehicle was insured with the present appellant- Insurance Company, and therefore, all respondents therein were jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

sentences.text: 3. Driver of the offending vehicle filed his written statement denying all allegations and contending that no accident occurred due to his vehicle.

Owner of offending vehicle remained absent and was proceeded ex parte.
4.

The appellant-Insurance Company also filed its written statement denying the factum of accident and further contending that FIR was lodged after six days in collusion with respondents No.2 and 3- driver and owner of offending vehicle to secure false compensation.
It was also pleaded that the driver did not possess a valid driving licence and that the alleged insurance policy was a xerox copy not issued by the appellant.

It was asserted that appellant never insured the vehicle bearing registration No. MP-04-J-5462 for the period from 04.11.2011 to 03.11.2012, and hence, no liability could be fastened upon it.
5.

After considering the pleadings, framing issues, and evaluating oral and documentary evidence,
the Claims Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2, that the vehicle was owned by respondent No.3, and that appellant-Insurance Company was liable being the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Consequently, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs. 32,500/- with interest @ 7% per annum jointly and severally against respondents therein.

6. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned award, learned counsel of appellant contended that the Claims Tribunal erred in accepting a xerox copy of the insurance policy without insisting upon production of the original.

It is urged that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28093 3 MA-379-2016 the appellant never issued any policy in favour of owner of offending vehicle and that the Claims Tribunal wrongly presumed its validity.
It was further submitted that there was an unexplained delay of six days in lodging the FIR, which ought to have discredited the claimant's version.

It is,
therefore, contended that the impugned award is contrary to law and deserves to be set aside.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal, it is observed that the police had registered a criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle and, after investigation, filed a charge-sheet against him.
8.

It is a settled principle of law that once the police register an offence against the driver of the offending vehicle and submit a charge-sheet after investigation, a presumption arises regarding the involvement and negligence of the said driver.
Such presumption is, of course, rebuttable, but in the absence of any rebuttal evidence, the Tribunal is justified in relying upon it.

9. Mere delay in lodging the FIR cannot be treated as fatal to the case of the claimant, especially when satisfactory explanation has been furnished and the accident itself stands proved by cogent evidence.

The burden to disprove such presumption lies upon the person alleging false implication,
but in the present case, neither the driver nor the owner of the offending vehicle appeared before the Tribunal or entered the witness box to rebut the evidence of the claimant.
10. The appellant-Insurance Company has contended that the insurance policy relied upon by the Claims Tribunal was only a xerox copy and not proved in accordance with law.
However, it is also a United India Insurance Co.Ltd.

Thr. vs Bharat Singh Lodhi on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175102445/
2 settled legal position that the onus lies upon the Insurance Company to establish that there was no valid policy in existence or that there was a breach of its terms and conditions.

In the present case,
the appellant failed to produce any record, evidence or witness from its NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28093 4 MA-379-2016 office to substantiate its plea that no such policy was ever issued.
In absence of such proof, the Claims Tribunal was justified in accepting the insurance coverage and holding the insurer liable.
11. In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court finds no illegality, perversity, or material irregularity in the findings recorded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

The impugned award is just,
proper and based on sound appreciation of evidence.
12. Accordingly, the appeal filed by the appellant-Insurance Company fails and is hereby dismissed.

The impugned Award dated 19.01.2016 passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Karera, District Shivpuri in Claim Case No.06 of 2014 is hereby affirmed.
